svg.title: Ordering and backpressure
svg.text: Backpressure: Black Friday at the warehouse
Order only where it is needed, and let queues absorb the spikes your downstream systems cannot.
A. The bus does not promise order: make consumers tolerant
A late v1 after v3 fails the condition and is dropped on purpose.
B. A consumer that truly needs order: FIFO from the stream
Order is kept inside each message group. Different orders run in
parallel, so throughput grows with the number of active orders.
One stuck message blocks only its own group (one order), not
the queue. Use a FIFO DLQ, or the group stays blocked until
Do not put a FIFO queue after the bus and expect order: the bus
may already have reordered the events. Order must be kept from
the source (the stream) to the consumer.
20 workers x 200 ms per call = 100 calls/s. The queue grows instead of the warehouse falling over.
Use the event source mapping MaximumConcurrency, not low reserved concurrency: throttled
invocations send messages back to the queue and burn receive counts into the DLQ.
minutes from the start of the sale
Alarm: ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage > 45 min during sale events (> 5 min on normal days).
The saga waits on a task token with a 48-hour timeout, so a slow warehouse never cancels an order.
